subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden mixed trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` suppression, and what boundary should separate silent-intent internal text from legitimate substantive replies that append or mention the token?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve some mixed trailing-token replies, while the report asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; choosing that boundary changes shared reply-delivery semantics.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define a shared silent-intent classifier that suppresses internal/status preambles while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then use it across delivery paths.

options.title: Use blanket trailing-token suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` token and accept that some currently visible replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, reasoning-prefixed, and scoped path cases are suppressed, leaving broad mixed-content suppression out of scope.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define a shared silent-intent classifier that suppresses internal/status preambles while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then use it across delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-history routing signal for the shared auto-reply policy files and earlier mixed-token behavior.
